notes: THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT DOCUMENT IN PHASE 5 AND IT SHOULD BE READ BEFORE THE SCHEMA IS FROZEN. Everything the certificate primitive in section 4.4 was designed for is here — a named person, a named issuer, an issue date, an expiry — and so is a set of behaviours that the primitive as drafted cannot express. Those are set out in full in competency_group_notes.md; the four that matter most are summarised here because they are properties of THIS document. (1) VALIDITY IS DERIVED, NOT STORED. 'Certifications are valid only for the remaining period of a candidate's training record. For example, if a training record has three months of validity remaining, the certification will only be issued for that duration' (p5). The certificate's valid_until is the MINIMUM of its own two-year ceiling and the expiry of a separate underlying credential. A schema that stores valid_until as a plain date will hold a value that is silently wrong the moment the underlying training record lapses — and the document is explicit about the consequence: 'If a valid training record/credential expires, the certification is rendered invalid, and the individual may not perform lifeguard duties until updated training records are provided' (p5). A lifeguard can therefore be un-certified today by an event recorded on a different row. (2) CERTIFICATES DEPEND ON OTHER CERTIFICATES. A lifeguard needs an accredited lifeguard qualification AND a DCAS-approved BLS/First Aid/CPR/AED qualification AND, where DHA requires it, a valid Occupational Health Card. An instructor needs all of that PLUS a valid lifeguard certificate from the same certifying agency PLUS a BLS/first aid TRAINER qualification. These are prerequisite edges between certificate rows, and section 4.4 has no way to draw them. (3) RENEWAL RUNS FROM THE OLD EXPIRY, NOT FROM THE EXAM. 'Regardless of the date of the renewal examination within that 2-month period, the new two-year certification period begins from the date not later than the expiry date of the candidate's initial certification' (p14). Computing valid_until as issued_on plus 24 months — the obvious implementation — silently grants up to two extra months of validity. This is a live mis-issuance risk, not a modelling nicety. (4) EXPIRY IS A CLIFF, NOT A WARNING. 'There is no grace period after their certification expires. Candidates whose certification has lapsed must take a full course followed by theory and practical exams to be certified again' (p15). Recertification is only available inside the two months before expiry; one day late and the cost jumps from a renewal exam to a full course. That makes the due-soon window a hard business rule with money attached, and it is exactly the thing this product should be selling. MODULE KIND = COMPLIANCE, and it is the cleanest compliance case in the whole Phase 5 set. There is no interpretation involved: an aquatic facility either has, on shift, lifeguards holding unexpired certificates of the right specialty for the water they are watching, or it does not. Both the credential and the specialty matching are objectively checkable, and the document requires the evidence to be on hand — 'Lifeguards and employers must ensure certification cards/qualifications and related records are available at all times for inspection by local authorities' (p17). VALIDITY VERSUS INTERVAL, checked specifically per the Phase 3 lesson: unlike all five Phase 3 certificate guidelines, this document states A REAL VALIDITY PERIOD — two years, stated three separate times (p13 'valid for two years', p14 'shall not have more than two years validity', p17 'valid for a maximum period of two years from the final accreditation approval date'). It ALSO states intervals (4 hours of in-service training per month, quarterly reporting) and deadlines (30 days to pass both exams, 3 months' grace on proof of passing pending the card). All three kinds are present and are recorded separately below. AN INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY, FLAGGED NOT RESOLVED: p13 says the certificate is 'valid for two years, renewed after taking a renewal course', p17 point 8 says 'valid for a maximum period of two years FROM THE FINAL ACCREDITATION APPROVAL DATE', and p5 says validity is capped by the remaining training-record period. Three different anchor dates for the same clock — issue, final accreditation approval, and the underlying record's expiry. The two-year ceiling is certain; WHICH DATE IT RUNS FROM is not, and the app must not assume. Only DM can close this. A SECOND ONE: p14 says instructor certification 'is valid as per the international organization standard' and then, two paragraphs later, that it 'shall not have more than two years validity'. The two-year cap governs as the stricter and more specific statement, but the deferral to the international body's standard means the real figure may be shorter for some awarding bodies. EDITION: version V 2 and issue date 14 January 2025 are from the cover, which prints them in long form ('14th January 2025'), so there is NO day/month ambiguity and confidence is high — this is not a rule-2 case. Superseded issue date 12 November 2024, meaning V1 lasted about two months. The source_url sits under /uploads/2025/02/, a month after the stated issue date, the usual upload-versus-issue offset. Note the code DM-HSD-S1 carries no GU number and no guideline number at all; guideline_no is null, which the standards registry must accommodate. SCOPE NOTE: 'Pool attendant' is expressly defined as NOT a lifeguard qualification and 'not covered by this document' (p8). A facility staffing pool attendants is not thereby staffing lifeguards, and the module must not count them.

competencies.role: Qualified Pool Lifeguard (water deeper than 1.5 m, including water parks)
competencies.requirement: Meet the candidate prerequisites (age per UAE law; swim 100 m nonstop comfortably; surface dive and recover a 4 kg weight at 3 m or the deepest depth of the facility where they will lifeguard; tread water at least 5 minutes). Hold valid approved International Lifeguard Organization training and BLS (Health Care Provider CPR) unless the lifeguard course includes them, with the BLS/First Aid/Emergency response/CPR curriculum approved by DCAS or taught by a DCAS-approved training centre. Hold a valid Occupational Health Card where the Dubai Health Authority requires one. Comply with the Substance Abuse Policy and sign the Code of Ethics. Pass the Core written/oral examination (all candidates, regardless of specialty) and the Pool specialty examination, plus the practical examination in the matching specialty. Lifeguards assigned to specialised environments such as water parks must undergo additional examinations at the specific facility where they will work or teach, with the certification body defining the scope.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC) — an international lifeguard organization; BLS/First Aid/CPR/AED portion approved by Dubai Corporation for Ambulance Services (DCAS)
competencies.renewal_requirement: Recertification by passing the recertification written/oral AND practical examinations, completed at any time within the two months before expiry, and continuing to meet the local health authority's medical requirements. Two attempts are allowed before expiry; candidates unsuccessful after two attempts must undertake the full course. Renewal training per the international certification agency must be taken regardless of how much experience the candidate can prove. The new two-year period begins from a date not later than the expiry of the initial certification, NOT from the renewal exam date. NO GRACE PERIOD: once lapsed, a full course plus theory and practical exams is required. Validity is additionally capped by the remaining validity of the underlying training record.
competencies.trigger_event: initial certification; and within the two months before each expiry
competencies.source_quote: The certificate shall be valid for two years, renewed after taking a renewal course. In addition to that lifeguards should attend a minimum of documented 4 hr. in-service training per month. Candidates have 30 days from the examination day to pass both theory and practical exams. Recertification: A lifeguard certificate shall not have more than two year's validity. For recertification, candidates must complete all recertification requirements at any time within two months prior to their certification's expiry date.

competencies.role: Qualified Shallow Water Lifeguard (maximum 1.5 m depth)
competencies.requirement: As for the Pool Lifeguard, but with the shallow-water prerequisites: swim 50 m nonstop comfortably, and surface dive to recover a 4 kg weight at 1.5 m. Certified with an express limitation to a maximum 1.5 m pool depth, which may be a water park facility or a shallow swimming pool. Must pass the Core examination plus the Shallow Water specialty examination and the matching practical.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC); BLS/First Aid/CPR/AED portion approved by DCAS
competencies.renewal_requirement: Identical recertification regime to the Pool Lifeguard: two-month pre-expiry window, two attempts, no grace period, new period running from the old expiry date.
competencies.trigger_event: initial certification; and within the two months before each expiry
competencies.source_quote: Qualified Shallow water lifeguard: A qualified lifeguard who has been trained and certified with limitation to the maximum 1.5 m depth of the pool which he/she will be assigned to work in. This might be in water park facility or a shallow depth swimming pool.

competencies.requirement: As for the Pool Lifeguard, but with the beach prerequisites: swim 200 m nonstop comfortably, surface dive and recover a 4 kg weight at 5 m, and tread water at least 10 minutes. Must pass the Core examination plus the Beach specialty examination and the matching practical. The document notes beach lifeguards typically carry broader responsibilities because of the unique hazards and environmental challenges of beach settings.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC); BLS/First Aid/CPR/AED portion approved by DCAS
competencies.renewal_requirement: Identical recertification regime to the Pool Lifeguard.
competencies.trigger_event: initial certification; and within the two months before each expiry
competencies.source_quote: 2. Swim continuously in a strong manner for: ... c. 200m nonstop in a comfortable manner, for a Beach/Waterfront Lifeguard. 3. Perform a surface dive and recover a 4 kg weight at a depth of: ... c. 5m for Beach/Waterfront Lifeguard. 4. Tread water for at least: ... b. 10 minutes for Beach lifeguards.

competencies.role: Lagoons and other water features Lifeguard
competencies.requirement: Named in the scope as one of the five categories the scheme applies to. NO SEPARATE PREREQUISITES, EXAMINATION SPECIALTY OR DEPTH RULE IS GIVEN FOR THIS CATEGORY ANYWHERE IN THE DOCUMENT — the specialty examinations are enumerated as exactly three groups (shallow water, pool, beach) on p12, and lagoons appear in neither that list nor the prerequisite table. The category must therefore be mapped onto shallow water, pool or beach by depth, but the document does not say to do so and does not say by whom.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC)
competencies.renewal_requirement: Presumed identical to the other categories; not separately stated.
competencies.trigger_event: initial certification; and within the two months before each expiry
competencies.source_quote: This scheme applies to all types of water lifeguards, including: 1- Swimming Pool Lifeguards 2- Beach Lifeguards 3- Shallow Water Lifeguards 4- Lagoons & other water features Lifeguards 5- Lifeguard Instructors
competencies.note: GAP FLAGGED, NOT FILLED. Recorded at medium confidence because the role is unambiguously in scope but its requirements are absent. This gap matters more than it looks for this business: lagoons are named explicitly, and the client base includes lagoon operators. Do NOT infer that the pool specialty covers a lagoon — depth, visibility and rescue distances differ, and inferring here would be the confident wrong answer section 7.4 forbids. Only DM can close it.

competencies.requirement: Be at least 18 years of age. Hold proof of lifeguard qualification in the field they wish to instruct, with the SAME training agency, and hold a valid lifeguard certificate from the same certifying agency. Hold a valid BLS and first aid qualification approved by EIAC, and a valid BLS/first aid TRAINER qualification. Provide proof of experience as a lifeguard. Strong command of English and a Train The Trainer certificate. Hold a valid Occupational Health Card from a valid approved international lifeguard organization in the place they intend to work. Comply with the Substance Abuse Policy. Pass the written examination in the intended specialty — instructors must take the WRITTEN form; the oral option is not available to them — and pass the practical examination. Training must be backed by probationary co-teaching and mentoring with a fully qualified and experienced trainer.
competencies.issuing_body: Certification Body accredited by EIAC / international lifeguard organization (Awarding Body); BLS and first aid qualification approved by EIAC
competencies.renewal_requirement: Recertification within the two months before expiry, by passing the recertification written/oral and practical examinations and continuing to meet the local health authority's medical requirements. Two attempts, then the full course. No grace period. NOTE THE INTERNAL CONFLICT recorded in the file notes: the document first says instructor certification 'is valid as per the international organization standard' and then that it 'shall not have more than two years validity'. 24 months is recorded as the ceiling; the operative figure may be shorter for a given awarding body.
competencies.trigger_event: initial certification; and within the two months before each expiry
competencies.source_quote: Lifeguard Instructor/Trainer is valid as per the international organization standard after taking a renewal course. In addition to that lifeguard instructors should attend and deliver a minimum of documented 4 hr. in-service training per month. Re-certification: Lifeguard instructor certificate shall not have more than two years validity.

competencies.requirement: The top of the progression, which the document states as Lifeguard, then Instructor/Trainer, then Instructor Trainer. Instructor Trainers are authorised by an approved awarding body. The document expressly places the detail outside its own scope — the definitions table footnote marks this route 'Not applicable for the scope of this document, done by the international organization' — so no prerequisites, examination or validity are stated here. Training centres must nonetheless keep copies of their certificates including expiry dates.
competencies.issuing_body: Approved awarding body / international lifeguard organization — expressly outside the scope of this DM document
competencies.source_quote: Lifeguard instructor trainer: The progression is Lifeguard-Instructor/Trainer-Instructor Trainer. Instructor Trainers are authorized by an awarding body who is approved. ... *** Not applicable for the scope of this document, done by the international organization (p9)

competencies.requirement: Assesses the competency of the lifeguard candidate as part of the certification requirement. MUST BE INDEPENDENT, for both theory and practical. Must be an examiner certified by the same Accredited Certification Body that gave the candidate their training — 'Candidates shall only be assessed as per the training they have been given by the same Accredited Certification Body certified examiner'. For oral assessments the examiner must use the Accredited Certification Body's official question bank and must record the questions asked of each candidate by referencing question numbers in the assessment form. No qualification, experience threshold or validity is stated for the examiner beyond independence and CB certification. Accredited certification bodies must maintain and submit a list of Approved Lifeguard Examiners to EIAC.
competencies.issuing_body: Accredited Certification Body (EIAC-accredited international lifeguard organization)
competencies.renewal_requirement: None stated. Examiner status is maintained through the CB's list submitted quarterly to EIAC rather than by an expiring credential — recorded null honestly.
competencies.source_quote: 4-6 The Summative Assessment. The examiner (for both theory and practical) must be independent. Candidates may be examined individually or in a group of no more than five candidates for the practical part. ... For oral assessments, an official question bank by the Accredited Certification Body must be used and the examiner must record questions asked of each candidate by referencing the question numbers in the assessment form. In either case records for both practical and theory sections shall be kept for the validity period of the certification. Candidates shall only be assessed as per the training they have been given by the same Accredited Certification Body certified examiner.

competencies.requirement: An international lifeguard organization granted accreditation by EIAC. Companies offering certification services must comply with all the scheme's requirements and receive EIAC approval. The CB defines the scope of the additional facility-specific examinations for specialised environments such as water parks, specifies the practical skills in each category and the teaching method for each skill, provides the official examinations (multiple choice format) and the official oral question bank, and certifies the examiners. May set prerequisites EXCEEDING those in the scheme but never falling short of them.
competencies.renewal_requirement: No accreditation validity period is stated in this document; EIAC's own accreditation cycle governs and is not reproduced. What IS stated is a continuing quarterly reporting duty to the Certification Bodies Accreditation Section and to EIAC. Recorded null honestly rather than assuming an ISO-style cycle.
competencies.source_quote: Companies offering certification services must comply with all outlined requirements and receive EIAC approval. (p5) Prerequisites, set by the accredited certification body, may exceed those listed above, but may not fall short of it. (p10)

competencies.role: Approved Training Program / Provider (ATP) and training centre
competencies.requirement: Training programs must be approved and certified as such by an international lifeguard organization (Awarding Body) AND accredited by EIAC. All training must follow an EIAC-endorsed approved program. The program must hold: an internationally accredited BLS/First Aid program approved by DCAS; a fully integrated textbook covering water rescue techniques, spinal management, first aid, healthcare provider BLS, emergency oxygen support and AED training; a MEDICAL SUPERVISOR/REPRESENTATIVE who ensures the curriculum meets the minimum standard set by the International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation (ILCOR); a fully integrated course transitioning from water to dry skills; a scheme of work and detailed lesson plans for each qualification; training records for each trainee; attendance sheets signed by instructor and/or trainees (electronic accepted); testing forms and testing result forms of the international training organization; course evaluation forms; health and safety standards and hygiene policies for training and testing including equipment cleaning checklists; and VALID LIABILITY INSURANCE held either by the training program or by individual instructors.
competencies.issuing_body: International lifeguard organization (Awarding Body) plus Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC)
competencies.renewal_requirement: No approval validity period stated. Continuing duties are quarterly reporting to EIAC and record keeping. Recorded null honestly.
competencies.source_quote: 4-13 Approved Lifeguard Training Programs/Providers (ATP). Training Programs must be approved and certified as such by an international lifeguard organization (Awarding Body). Additionally, they must be accredited by Emirates International Accreditation Center (EIAC). (p18) A Medical Supervisor/Representative who ensures the curriculum meets the minimum standard as outlined by International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation (ILCOR) ... Valid liability insurance either by the training program, or individual instructors. (p19)

competencies.requirement: Named only as a record the facility management must keep — 'Record of a certified pool plant operator' — in the section 4-12 list of records required by local technical guidelines. NO requirements, issuing body, examination or validity for this role appear anywhere in this document; it is a cross-reference to the HSD technical guidelines on public swimming pools. Recorded so the role is not lost, because a facility compliance view will need it and it will otherwise fall between two guidelines.
competencies.source_quote: The facility management shall keep a record for the following as set by local technical guidelines: ... 7 Record of a certified pool plant operator

limits.parameter_label: Maximum validity of a lifeguard or lifeguard instructor certificate
limits.display: shall not have more than two year's validity
limits.qualifier_rule: A CEILING, not a fixed term. The actual validity is the lesser of two years and the remaining validity of the candidate's underlying training record, so a certificate may legitimately be issued for as little as a few months. See the file notes: this is the single most important structural finding for the schema.
limits.source_quote: A lifeguard certificate shall not have more than two year's validity. (p13) Lifeguard instructor certificate shall not have more than two years validity. (p14) Lifeguard certificates are valid for a maximum period of two years from the final accreditation approval date. (p17)
limits.note: Inclusive at two years by the 'not more than' glyph. Stated three times, with THREE DIFFERENT ANCHOR DATES across those statements (issue, final accreditation approval date, and the training record's remaining period). The two-year ceiling is certain; the anchor is not, and the app must not pick one silently.

limits.parameter_label: Window before expiry within which recertification must be completed
limits.display: at any time within two months prior to their certification's expiry date
limits.qualifier_rule: Recertification may be completed at any point inside this window and NOT outside it. Two examination attempts are permitted within the window; failing both means the full course. Regardless of when in the window the renewal exam is passed, the new two-year period runs from a date not later than the original expiry — so renewing early costs the candidate nothing, and there is no incentive to leave it late.
limits.source_quote: For recertification, candidates must complete all recertification requirements at any time within two months prior to their certification's expiry date. (p13) Regardless of the date of the renewal examination within that 2-month period, the new two-year certification period begins from the date not later than the expiry date of the candidate's initial certification. (p14)
limits.note: This is the single most commercially valuable number in the Phase 5 corpus for this product. It defines a hard 60-day action window with a severe, quantified penalty for missing it — 'There is no grace period after their certification expires. Candidates whose certification has lapsed must take a full course' (p15). A due-soon alert at 60 days before expiry is not a nicety here; it is the difference between a renewal exam and a full re-course for the client.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum documented in-service training per month
limits.display: a minimum of documented 4 hr. in-service training per month
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to certified lifeguards (attend) and to lifeguard instructors (attend AND deliver). Must be DOCUMENTED, which makes it auditable and gives the module a monthly recurring evidence item between the two-yearly certification events.
limits.source_quote: In addition to that lifeguards should attend a minimum of documented 4 hr. in-service training per month. (p13) In addition to that lifeguard instructors should attend and deliver a minimum of documented 4 hr. in-service training per month. (p14)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Note the verb is 'should', not 'shall', which weakens it relative to the certification requirements — but the document requires the training to be documented, so evidence is expected regardless. The most frequent recurring obligation in the whole Phase 5 set.

limits.parameter_label: Deadline to pass both theory and practical examinations
limits.display: Candidates have 30 days from the examination day to pass both theory and practical exams
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to lifeguard candidates and to instructor candidates alike. The two examinations may be taken in either order; the clock runs from the examination day.
limits.source_quote: Candidates have 30 days from the examination day to pass both theory and practical exams. (p13) Candidates may take their practical exams after they successfully passed the written exams, it can be in either order. Candidates have 30 days from the examination day to pass both theory and practical exams/s. (p14)
limits.note: Inclusive by the plain reading of 'have 30 days'. Ambiguity worth noting: 'from the examination day' does not say which examination — the first one sat, presumably, but where a candidate sits theory and practical on different days the start of the clock is not fixed by the text.

limits.parameter_label: Validity of proof of passing pending receipt of the certification card
limits.display: Proof of passing the assessment is valid for up to 3 months from the date of passing, until the original card/qualification is received
limits.qualifier_rule: A bridging credential: it permits the lifeguard to work between passing and receiving the laminated ID card, and it expires whether or not the card has arrived.
limits.source_quote: 1. Proof of passing the assessment is valid for up to 3 months from the date of passing, until the original card/qualification is received.
limits.note: Inclusive by the 'up to 3 months' phrasing. Operationally important and easy to miss: a compliance view that only recognises issued cards will show a false gap for up to three months after a valid pass, and one that never expires the interim proof will show a false pass after three months. Both failure modes are real.

limits.parameter_label: Depth threshold separating shallow water from pool lifeguarding
limits.display: shallow water means that the depth is maximum 1.5m; Pools means that the depth is more than 1.5m
limits.qualifier_rule: THE KEY SCOPING NUMBER FOR SPECIALTY MATCHING. At or below 1.5 m a Shallow Water certificate suffices; above 1.5 m a Pool certificate is required. A Shallow Water Lifeguard posted to water deeper than 1.5 m is working outside their certification, which is a checkable non-compliance and probably the highest-value single check this module can perform.
limits.source_quote: a. 1.5m for a Shallow Water Lifeguard, where shallow water means that the depth is maximum 1.5m. b. 3m, or to the deepest depth of the facility in which they will be lifeguarding for a Pool Lifeguard, where Pools means that the depth is more than 1.5m
limits.note: The boundary is clean with no gap and no overlap: 'maximum 1.5m' is inclusive and 'more than 1.5m' is exclusive, so exactly 1.5 m is shallow water. Rare clarity — most band boundaries in this corpus are not this well drawn.

limits.parameter_label: Prerequisite continuous swim — Shallow Water Lifeguard
limits.display: 50m nonstop in a comfortable manner, for a Shallow Water Lifeguards in under 1.5m depth
limits.qualifier_rule: Entry prerequisite to enrol on a lifeguard course, not an ongoing fitness standard. The accredited certification body may set higher prerequisites but may not fall short of these.
limits.source_quote: 2. Swim continuously in a strong manner for: a. 50m nonstop in a comfortable manner, for a Shallow Water Lifeguards in under 1.5m depth.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Note the depth wording here is 'under 1.5m' whereas the definitions and the dive prerequisite say 'maximum 1.5m' — a minor internal inconsistency about whether exactly 1.5 m is shallow water. The definition on p8 and the dive clause both say maximum, so 1.5 m inclusive is taken as correct.

limits.display: 100m nonstop in a comfortable manner, for a Pool Lifeguard in over 1.5m depth
limits.qualifier_rule: Entry prerequisite to enrol on a lifeguard course.
limits.source_quote: b. 100m nonstop in a comfortable manner, for a Pool Lifeguard in over 1.5m depth

limits.parameter_label: Prerequisite continuous swim — Beach / Waterfront Lifeguard
limits.display: 200m nonstop in a comfortable manner, for a Beach/Waterfront Lifeguard
limits.qualifier_rule: Entry prerequisite to enrol on a lifeguard course.
limits.source_quote: c. 200m nonstop in a comfortable manner, for a Beach/Waterfront Lifeguard.

limits.parameter_label: Weight to be recovered on the prerequisite surface dive
limits.qualifier_rule: Common to all three specialties; only the depth differs (1.5 m shallow water, 3 m or the deepest depth of the facility for pool, 5 m beach).
limits.source_quote: 3. Perform a surface dive and recover a 4 kg weight at a depth of:
limits.note: A fixed specification rather than a bound; recorded with min_val 4 since the CB may exceed but not fall short of any prerequisite.

limits.parameter_label: Prerequisite surface dive depth — Pool Lifeguard
limits.display: 3m, or to the deepest depth of the facility in which they will be lifeguarding
limits.qualifier_rule: FACILITY-DEPENDENT: the requirement is the GREATER of 3 m and the deepest depth of the facility where the lifeguard will work. A lifeguard qualified against a 3 m pool is not automatically qualified for a 5 m dive tank, and this is a per-posting check rather than a one-time credential check.
limits.source_quote: b. 3m, or to the deepest depth of the facility in which they will be lifeguarding for a Pool Lifeguard, where Pools means that the depth is more than 1.5m
limits.note: Inclusive minimum, but the operative value varies by site. This, together with the water-park facility-specific examination requirement on p4, means a lifeguard's certification is partly TIED TO A SITE — another thing a flat certificate row against subject_user_id cannot express. See competency_group_notes.md.

limits.parameter_label: Prerequisite surface dive depth — Shallow Water Lifeguard
limits.qualifier_rule: Entry prerequisite; matches the shallow water depth ceiling.
limits.source_quote: a. 1.5m for a Shallow Water Lifeguard, where shallow water means that the depth is maximum 1.5m.

Prerequisite tread water duration — Pool Lifeguard

limits.qualifier_rule: Entry prerequisite. NOTE: the tread-water prerequisite list names only pool and beach lifeguards — no figure is given for shallow water lifeguards, and no statement is made that they are exempt. A genuine gap in the table, not an omission in this extraction.
limits.source_quote: 4. Tread water for at least: a. 5 minutes for Pool lifeguards. b. 10 minutes for Beach lifeguards.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum age for a lifeguard instructor candidate
limits.display: Be at least 18 years of age
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to instructor candidates. Lifeguard candidates themselves have no numeric age requirement — the scheme says only 'Be of age according to UAE laws', deferring to labour law rather than setting a figure.
limits.source_quote: 1. Be at least 18 years of age. (instructor prerequisites, p13) 1. Be of age according to UAE laws (lifeguard candidate prerequisites, p10)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. The lifeguard-candidate age is a delegation, not a number, and must not be filled in with 18 by analogy.

limits.display: Candidates may be examined individually or in a group of no more than five candidates for the practical part
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to the practical section of the summative assessment only.
limits.source_quote: Candidates may be examined individually or in a group of no more than five candidates for the practical part.
limits.note: Inclusive at five by the 'no more than' glyph.

limits.parameter_label: Rescue tubes required per training candidate
limits.display: One rescue tube for each three candidates or as per the international organization scheme
limits.qualifier_rule: Training centre equipment minimum. THE CONFLICT RULE IS STATED EXPLICITLY AND IS UNUSUALLY HELPFUL: 'Awarding Body may define Instructor to candidate or equipment to candidate ratios. If a conflict exists, the greater requirements shall be used.' So where the awarding body is stricter, the awarding body governs — the DM figure is a floor, never a ceiling.
limits.source_quote: Training centers must have the following, as minimum, training equipment and materials (Note: Awarding Body may define Instructor to candidate or equipment to candidate ratios. If a conflict exists, the greater requirements shall be used): One rescue tube for each three candidates or as per the international organization scheme
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Other stated per-candidate items are one resuscitation pocket mask with one-way valve per candidate for water rescue exercises, one resuscitation face shield per candidate, and one training bandage, one triangular bandage and one pair of gloves per candidate.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum body straps on a training spine board
limits.display: Spine board with min. of three body straps and head immobilization
limits.source_quote: Spine board with min. of three body straps and head immobilization
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Head immobilisation is required in addition to the straps.

obligations.cadence_note: Two years, but the app MUST NOT compute the next due date as issued_on plus 24 months. Three rules override that: (a) validity is capped by the remaining validity of the underlying training record, so the real expiry may be far sooner; (b) recertification must be completed inside the two months BEFORE expiry, so the actionable due date is expiry minus 60 days; (c) on renewal the new two-year period runs from a date not later than the previous expiry, not from the exam date, so periods do not drift. Getting (c) wrong over-grants validity, which is a mis-issuance, not a cosmetic bug.
obligations.trigger_event: certification expiry approaching (window opens two months before expiry); lapse of the underlying training record or BLS/first aid credential, which invalidates the certification immediately
obligations.applies_to: Certified lifeguards (shallow water, pool, beach, lagoons) and lifeguard instructors — recertification by passing the recertification written/oral and practical examinations and continuing to meet the local health authority's medical requirements
obligations.source_quote: The certificate shall be valid for two years, renewed after taking a renewal course. ... A lifeguard certificate shall not have more than two year's validity. For recertification, candidates must complete all recertification requirements at any time within two months prior to their certification's expiry date. This includes: Passing the Recertification Written/Oral and practical Examination(s); Continuing to meet medical requirements by the local health authority. (p13) All candidates are allowed to pass two attempts to pass their renewal theory and practical assessment exams before their certification expires. Candidates who are unsuccessful after two attempts must undertake the full course. Regardless of the date of the renewal examination within that 2-month period, the new two-year certification period begins from the date not later than the expiry date of the candidate's initial certification. (p14) There is no grace period after their certification expires. Candidates whose certification has lapsed must take a full course followed by theory and practical exams to be certified again. (p15)

obligations.cadence_note: Monthly, at least 4 documented hours. The highest-frequency obligation in the Phase 5 set and the one that keeps the module alive between two-yearly certification events. Lifeguards attend; instructors attend AND deliver. Must be documented, so each month produces an evidence artefact. Note the verb is 'should' rather than 'shall', so this should be surfaced as a tracked commitment rather than a regulatory breach when missed.
obligations.applies_to: Certified lifeguards and lifeguard instructors — minimum 4 hours documented in-service training per month
obligations.source_quote: In addition to that lifeguards should attend a minimum of documented 4 hr. in-service training per month. (p13) In addition to that lifeguard instructors should attend and deliver a minimum of documented 4 hr. in-service training per month. (p14)

obligations.cadence_note: Quarterly, and there are TWO distinct quarterly reports with different senders, recipients and contents, which is why they are described together here but must not be collapsed into one task. Accredited certification bodies report to the Certification Bodies Accreditation Section on issued certificates, and separately to EIAC on approved examiners, examinations conducted, passed and failed candidates, and suspended or withdrawn certificates — the latter also due 'whenever any changes/additions were made to any', so it is event-driven as well as quarterly. Approved Training Centers report to EIAC on approved lifeguard trainers and training conducted (scope, number of trainees and their details, location, comments on trainee performance), and on completed training and the outcome for each participant.
obligations.trigger_event: end of each quarter; and, for certification bodies reporting to EIAC, whenever any change or addition is made
obligations.applies_to: Accredited certification bodies and Approved Training Centers
obligations.source_quote: 9. Accredited certification bodies must submit quarterly reports detailing issued certificates to the Certification Bodies Accreditation Section. 10. Approved Training Centers must submit quarterly reports detailing completed training and the outcomes for each participant. (p17) Approved Training Centers shall submit a quarterly report to EIAC which includes: 1 List of Approved Lifeguard Trainers, 2 Training Conducted details ... Accredited certification bodies need to submit a quarterly report to EIAC, or whenever any changes/additions were made to any, which includes: 1 List of Approved Lifeguard Examiners, 2 Examination conducted, 3 Passed & Failed Candidates. 4 Suspended or withdrawn Lifeguard certificates (p18)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing record-retention duty. Retention is expressed relative to the certificate rather than as a fixed term: summative assessment records for both practical and theory sections 'shall be kept for the validity period of the certification' — so retention is a moving target tied to another row's expiry, which is the same derived-date problem the certificate validity has. Training centres must additionally keep copies of the certificates INCLUDING EXPIRY DATES for lifeguards, lifeguard instructors and lifeguard instructor trainers. Lifeguards and employers must ensure cards and records are available AT ALL TIMES for inspection by local authorities. Mapped to 'reporting' as the closest term in the closed vocabulary; the duty is retain-and-produce-on-demand. Noted per rule 4.
obligations.applies_to: Training centres and employers — summative assessment records (theory and practical), copies of certificates with expiry dates for lifeguards, instructors and instructor trainers, signed Code of Ethics forms in each candidate file, and certification cards
obligations.source_quote: In either case records for both practical and theory sections shall be kept for the validity period of the certification. (p15) 6. Lifeguards and employers must ensure certification cards/qualifications and related records are available at all times for inspection by local authorities. (p17) All training centers shall keep copies of the certificates, which include the expiry date, and the validity of the certificate for the following personnel: Lifeguards, lifeguard instructors, Lifeguard instructor trainers. (p17-18) 9. Candidates are required to sign a code of ethics form and the training center shall keep the signed document in the candidate file. (p16)

obligations.cadence_note: NO INTERVAL STATED — a genuine and consequential null. Certified lifeguards 'must continue to meet physical requirements throughout their certification periods and attest to their agreement to this requirement in their applications', and recertification requires 'continuing to meet medical requirements by the local health authority'. So the obligation is continuous rather than periodic, discharged by attestation plus whatever cadence the local health authority sets — which this document does not reproduce. The related Occupational Health Card is required 'whenever required, as per Dubai Health Authority', again with no interval and no criteria for when it is required, so even the APPLICABILITY of that card cannot be determined from this document.
obligations.trigger_event: application; recertification; and continuously throughout the certification period
obligations.applies_to: Certified lifeguards and lifeguard instructors — medical questionnaire, medical statement and physician instruction; continuing physical fitness; valid Occupational Health Card where DHA requires one; evidence of non-compliance with medical requirements is a ground for revocation
obligations.source_quote: Medical questionnaire, medical statement, and physician instruction: Certified lifeguards must continue to meet physical requirements throughout their certification periods and attest to their agreement to this requirement in their applications. (p18) Whenever required, as per Dubai Health Authority, candidates must hold a valid Occupational Health Card (p13) 5. Evidence of non-compliance with medical requirements (revocation ground, p16)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing facility duty with no cadence. The number of lifeguards on duty 'should be appropriate for the size of the facility and number of bathers' — NO RATIO, NO FORMULA AND NO TABLE IS GIVEN, which is the largest single gap in this document for compliance purposes. Contrast GU131, which fixes H&S officer headcount against room count in a table and thereby supports a verdict. Here the headcount requirement is real but unquantified, so the app can record how many lifeguards were on duty and cannot judge whether it was enough. Only DM can close this. Lifesaving equipment (AED, oxygen, spinal board, rescue tube, first aid kit) must be available; lifeguards must have an unobstructed view and quick access to swimming areas, be properly trained and deployed, and stay vigilant and attentive.
obligations.applies_to: Aquatic facility operators — lifeguard numbers appropriate to facility size and bather load, adequate resources and supporting environment, lifesaving equipment availability, unobstructed sightlines and quick access
obligations.source_quote: 4-7 Facilities Duty of Care. ... Lifeguards must be properly trained, deployed, and always stay vigilant and attentive. Facilities must provide lifeguards with adequate resources and an environment that supports their duties. The number of lifeguards on duty should be appropriate for the size of the facility and number of bathers. Lifesaving equipment (AED, oxygen, spinal board, rescue tube, first aid kit) must be available. Lifeguards must have an unobstructed view and quick access to swimming areas. (p15)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing prohibition on task conflict, no cadence. Additional duties — water quality testing, monitoring filtration, checking chlorine levels, inspecting poolside amenities, record keeping, managing payments — may be assigned, but 'should never be performed when the lifeguard is responsible for swimmer protection', and the Code of Ethics binds the individual to the same rule. Lifeguards need proper training for any such additional duty. Worth surfacing because it is a scheduling rule an FM contractor can breach without noticing: rostering one lifeguard to test chlorine during their watch is a stated breach.
obligations.trigger_event: assignment of additional duties to a lifeguard on watch
obligations.applies_to: Lifeguards assigned duties beyond swimmer protection — water quality testing, pool maintenance, record keeping, payment handling
obligations.source_quote: These tasks, however, should never be performed when the lifeguard is responsible for swimmer protection. (p6) These 'additional duties' must not interfere with their primary responsibility of swimmer safety. (p6) 8. Not performing additional duties while assigned the duty of swimmer protection (Code of Ethics, p16) Lifeguards may also be assigned additional duties like water quality testing or pool maintenance, for which they need proper training. (p15)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing conduct requirement, no cadence. Certified lifeguards must comply with the Code of Ethics throughout their certification and must SIGN a code of ethics form, retained in the candidate file at the training centre. The Substance Abuse Policy prohibits prescribed or over-the-counter substances that would impair safe performance, including alcohol, illegal drugs and controlled substances including trace amounts, except where a licensed medical practitioner prescribes with prior knowledge of the lifeguard's history and career requirements and assurance of no adverse effect on duties. Mapped to 'process' as the closest vocabulary term; the duty is a signed undertaking plus ongoing conduct. Noted per rule 4.
obligations.trigger_event: certification; and continuously throughout the certification period
obligations.applies_to: All certified lifeguards — Code of Ethics (nine clauses covering non-discrimination, prioritising public and worker safety, protecting property and environment, escalating safety concerns, not violating DM safety regulations, not misrepresenting experience or capability, not misusing the certification card or organisation logo and returning the card on demand, and not performing additional duties while on swimmer protection) and the Substance Abuse Policy
obligations.source_quote: 4-9 Code of Ethics. Certified lifeguard must comply with Code of Ethics during their certification, as set forth below (p16) 4-15 Substance Abuse Policy. Lifeguards shall not use prescribed or over-the-counter substances that would impair their ability to perform their duties safely. (p20)

obligations.cadence_note: Event-driven, no cadence. Certification may be REVOKED on six stated grounds: period of certification exceeded without renewal; falsification of any information on documents submitted to the certifying authority or its agents; non-compliance with the Substance Abuse Policy; culpability in an accident during the certification period; non-compliance with medical requirements; non-compliance with the Code of Ethics. The list is expressly non-exhaustive ('shall include, but not be limited to'). A complaints procedure exists to ensure only valid and actionable complaints are investigated, with all parties able to document circumstances and respond. Mapped to 'process' as the closest vocabulary term; revocation and complaint handling have no exact type. Noted per rule 4. IMPORTANT FOR THE DATA MODEL: revocation means a certificate can cease to be valid before its expiry date, so validity is not a pure function of dates — a status field is required as well.
obligations.trigger_event: expiry without renewal; falsification; substance abuse; culpability in an accident; medical non-compliance; ethics breach; or a valid complaint
obligations.applies_to: Certified lifeguards and instructors — revocation of certification status, and the associated complaints procedure
obligations.source_quote: 4-8 Disciplinary Policy. Grounds for revocation of certification status shall include, but not be limited to, the following: 1. Period of certification exceeded without renewal. 2. Evidence of falsification of any information on any documents submitted to certifying authority or its agents. 3. Evidence of non-compliance with Substance Abuse Policy 4. Evidence of culpability in an accident during certification period 5. Evidence of non-compliance with medical requirements 6. Evidence of non-compliance with the Code of Ethics (p15-16)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing credential-integrity requirements, no cadence. Lifeguards may hold ONLY ONE certification card at a time. Electronic credentials may be accepted if they contain the necessary record and access to training details. Replacement or updated cards for additional specialties, or for retaking previously failed specialties, may be issued simultaneously. The card must carry: photo of the certified lifeguard or instructor, date of birth, certification date, EXPIRY DATE, examiner information, lifeguarding specialty, and the name and location of the training facility. That field list is effectively DM specifying the minimum schema for a people-certificate record and should be compared against section 4.4's columns — note that 'examiner information' and 'specialty' have no home in the current certificates table.
obligations.trigger_event: issue or replacement of a certification card
obligations.applies_to: Certification cards and records for lifeguards, instructors and instructor trainers
obligations.source_quote: 3. Lifeguards may hold only one certification card at a time. 4. Electronic credentials may be accepted if they contain the necessary record and access to training details. ... 7. Certification cards/records must include: Photo of the certified lifeguard (or instructor/trainer); Date of birth; Certification date; Expiry date; Examiner information; Lifeguarding specialty (e.g., shallow water, pool, or beach); Name and location of the training facility (p16-17)

obligations.cadence_note: Event-driven, no cadence. Recorded separately from the competency obligation because the assessment has its own independent integrity rules: the examiner must be independent for both theory and practical; groups of no more than five for the practical; official examinations from the certification agency in multiple choice format; oral administration permitted only where materials or exams are unavailable in a language the candidate understands or the candidate cannot read or write, with translator, special needs and online options also to be available; instructors must sit the written form. At the test site, candidates must bring photo identification (passport, government-issued driver's licence, or Emirates ID) plus an admission letter valid for the specific test date, and may be required to sign the test site roster.
obligations.applies_to: Lifeguard and lifeguard instructor candidates — Core examination (all candidates regardless of specialty) plus one or more Specialty examinations (shallow water, pool, beach), and a practical examination whose specialties must correspond to the written ones. Final scenarios must include in-water rescue, water exit and extrication, poolside and beach rescue, use of spinal board and rescue tube, and out-of-water first aid and BLS for adult, child and infants including AED and emergency oxygen kit use.
obligations.source_quote: All candidates are required to take the Core Examination, regardless of the Specialty(s) in which they wish to be certified. (p12) 4-5 Practical Exam. Final scenarios shall be administered to assess the competence level of the lifeguard candidate. (p12) The examiner (for both theory and practical) must be independent. (p15) In addition to an admission letter valid for the specific test date, candidates must bring photo identification to the test site on the day of the test administration. (p17)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing facility record-keeping duty with no cadence stated in THIS document — the cadences live in the local technical guidelines it defers to, principally the HSD Technical Guidelines on safety of public swimming pools. Recorded because it is the bridge between this people-competency module and the facility-side water quality modules, and because two of the seven items (daily emergency equipment checks, open and closing checklist) are plainly daily even though this document does not say so. A delegating obligation inside an otherwise self-contained compliance guideline.
obligations.applies_to: Aquatic facility management — records of: accidents and reportable incidents; chemical logbooks; bacterial analysis per HSD Technical Guidelines on safety of public swimming pools; maintenance records; open and closing checklist confirming visibility of the entire bottom; daily emergency equipment checks; and record of a certified pool plant operator
obligations.source_quote: The facility management shall keep a record for the following as set by local technical guidelines: 1 Accidents and reportable incidents 2 Chemical logbooks. 3 Bacterial analysis as per HSD Technical Guidelines on safety of public swimming pools 4 Maintenance records. 5 Open and closing check list - confirms visibility of the entire bottom. 6 Daily emergency equipment checks. 7 Record of a certified pool plant operator (p18)
